keyFindings.description: The head is `CONFLICTING`/`DIRTY` against main: 4 ahead, 33 behind, 14 two-sided conflicts (docs/kubernetes.md, internal/api/settings.go, internal/config/kubernetes.go and its test, internal/launcher/launcher.go and its test, and seven files under internal/runtime/sandbox/). GitHub computes no merge ref for a conflicting head and starts no `on: pull_request` workflow for it, so no check will ever report here. The cause is main's #2179, which rewrote the session-store configuration this change depends on and added a third kind, `cloudsql-iam`. The forward merge is the first item of the next round, and the architect has already decided what it contains: the refusal becomes `not pvc` rather than `must be postgres`, since `cloudsql-iam` keeps sessions off the disk as `postgres` does and `pvc` is the only kind this change makes unusable.

Security[untrusted-input]: the new session exporter writes host files at names the session database chooses. `session_copy` selects keys by textual prefix, strips the prefix, and uses the remainder in `mkdir -p "$(dirname "$dir/${path#"$prefix"}")"` and in the redirection `>"$dir/${path#"$prefix"}"`, with no containment check. A row whose key is `<prefix>../…` therefore writes outside `$evidence/transcripts`, and enough `../` components reach any path the operator can write. The row is writable from inside a pod: every role container mounts the session DSN (`internal/runtime/sandbox/manifest.go:574-578`, `:890-891`) and the harness creates that database as its owner (`stage4b-sandbox-tree.sh:3099-3104`), while a Legion agent reads untrusted text by design. The SQL side is sound — the path is a psql variable interpolated as a literal, the row precedes its parts in `start_offset` order, and an absent session fails rather than reading as an empty one — so this is the filesystem step alone. Reject `.`/`..` components and non-canonical or line-breaking keys, and check the resolved destination is under `$dir` before the `mkdir` and the redirection. ASVS v5.0.0-5.3.2.

The `pod-baseline` row still promises the stub agent's environment carries `OMP_SESSION_STORAGE=file`, against a check that now requires `ompsessions.SQLStorage` and its DSN pointer (`internal/runtime/sandbox/live_operator_test.go:179-183`). This is the third round it has stood: filed in round 3 and in my out-of-band note after it, and unfixed here. `:967`'s `setup-negative` row is the same pair — it still says the check "deletes the throwaway Sandbox and its PVC", where `live_setup_test.go:226` already notes the pod's own disk went with its pod.

keyFindings.description: The implementer's proof line no longer carries its own evidence: it says the commands, observations, heads and negative controls "are in `.legion/INFRA-80/implement.json` on this branch and in the thread replies on this pull request". Retro's last commit removes `.legion/<issue>/` from the head that merges, so the merged body cites a path the merged tree does not hold, and "the thread replies" is not a link. `skill://legion-worker/references/pr-body.md` asks the line itself to name the surface, the command or run id, what was observed, the head SHA and one negative control; the merger quotes that line into READY and the architect's acceptance reads it. Put the content back inline, or cite the commit that carries the handoff by SHA so the reference survives retro.

The ordinary issue fixture still defaults to a Sandbox-owned disk, so current-shape tests opt out with `withoutVolume` and the superseded shape is what a reader meets first. `cleanup_test.go:53-69` builds claims owned directly by Sandboxes and deletes them by hand while the test it serves claims to prove pod-owned deletion. Default the fixture to the shape this change makes and have the migration tests opt into the old one.

Prose still teaching the removed model, in six places this change owns: `scripts/e2e/README.md:1477` (the review pair reads the issue volume, where `stage4b-sandbox-tree.sh:1039-1041` reads the database); `stage4b-sandbox-tree.sh:5890-5891` (retaining the suspended Sandbox and volume, against its own deletion predicate at `:5904-5921`); `internal/runtime/sandbox/podkind.go:73-75` and `cleanup.go:72-75` (the issue Sandbox owns the volume, given as the general deletion invariant); `manifest_test.go:659-661` (logs, browser profiles and plugin generations outlive the pod); `relaunch_test.go:649-652` (the init container receives the session's location on the volume).

notAFinding.authorship: The code commit `862a809d38df` is authored by the review App and committed by the implement App, with the implementer's own `Omp-Session` trailer — a working copy split at a turn's start that carried the previous role's author. The architect first asked me to hold approval for it on the ground that the misattribution becomes permanent in main's history, then retracted. I verified the retraction rather than taking it: `gh api repos/sjawhar/legion` gives `allow_merge_commit: false`, `allow_rebase_merge: false`, `allow_squash_merge: true`, squash title `COMMIT_OR_PR_TITLE`, message `COMMIT_MESSAGES`. A squash writes one commit authored by the pull request's author, so the individual commit's author field never reaches main; the commit messages do, the author fields do not. No gate reads it either: `handoff_complete` refuses only a handoff commit another App authored, and the implement handoff `e0e738d2a079` is correctly authored. So it is not a finding and I did not request it. The habit it names — read the working copy's author at the turn's start, since a split inherits whichever role last held it — belongs in the retro note.

roundThreeVerification.note: Five of the six round-3 findings are fixed; I verified each at the head rather than from its reply. The sixth is the README row above.
verified: One SQL reader answers every pod-session consumer: claim_session_text → session_text (stage4b-sandbox-tree.sh:989-998), the reviewer and subagent keys through the same reader, and transcript collection through session_copy → session_text. No pod_exec cat of a transcript remains; the surviving local .jsonl reads are exported evidence and the intentionally file-backed operator controller.

The gap record is read against strandedGen, taken with the record and again once the confirming read answers, and a read the delete overtakes returns Uncertain (observe.go:109-124), which keeps the claim watched and charges no death. Both the write and the drop bump the counter, under the same mutex as the record (relaunch.go:614-637).
The census and the body name contract 37 throughout.
The cutover's audit step drops the label selector and says why no selector can answer (docs/kubernetes.md:1315-1341).
controllerPod's type comment describes a pod with no init container (podkind.go:282-287).
